sources.notes: 417 models at 687,878 bytes on 2026-08-26, re-probed at 687,941, so no size equality is asserted anywhere. minBytes is half the recorded size and minRecords 300 is a floor well under the 417 observed. Fast tier because cache-control gives a 300s TTL, and 15 minutes sits above that floor with headroom for edge age skew. Freshness kind none: this is a live catalogue, not a feed, and its own bytes drift between probes.

STILL PENDING, and not for want of a predicate. The arena extractor exists and was verified against two live 5.2 MB captures taken minutes apart: 1,846 projected record tuples, byte-unequal bodies, equal projections. It is blocked upstream of the predicate, at the health check. The live leaderboard carries window.__CF$cv$params, which is on the shared interstitial denylist, so checkHealth returns failed and the body is never written. That marker is not challenge-specific: Cloudflare injects the same beacon into ordinary proxied 200s, and test/fixtures/trap-interstitial.html carries __CF$cv$params and none of the other four markers, so dropping it from the denylist would leave that trap undetected. Resolving that tradeoff is a change to a module constant the spec deliberately made global, and it is not this task's to make. Predicate is extracted, not bytes, because two reviewers measured three per-request volatile regions independently and hours apart: a provisional userId UUIDv7 whose embedded ms timestamp decodes to the fetch instant, a 37 to 41 key posthogFlags map that re-rolls on any request because the visitor is anonymous, and a window.__CF$cv$params blob carrying the request's own cf-ray and clock, which changes on every response by construction. Masking only the first leaves the bodies unequal, so the predicate would fire every run and commit 5.2 MB forever into a history that is never rewritten. A mask list keyed on flag names also rots as arena ships experiments, so the predicate extracts the (publicName, displayName, rating, votes) tuples instead, wrapped in a 500-record floor because the payload is an undocumented framework shape and a silent drop to zero would report no change for ever. Size is per-request volatile too (5,235,684 to 5,235,887 observed), so minBytes is half the smaller observation and no fixed size is asserted. Freshness content/30 rather than the usual 90: the leaderboard gained models across both probe sessions and codename reveals are the entire point, so a quiet month means the extractor broke rather than that the industry stopped shipping. timeoutS 120 for a 5.2 MB body.

Predicate is extracted over sitemapDated, not bytes. Measured twice: two fetches four seconds apart on 2026-08-26 differed in 24 of 516 lastmod values with the loc set identical, and two fetches four minutes apart on 2026-08-31 differed in 25 of 522, the values oscillating backwards, which is two live edge-cache generations rather than a rebuild. A bytes predicate would commit 68 KB of that oscillation on every run into a history that is never rewritten. sitemapDated rather than sitemapLoc is the load-bearing choice: keying on the loc set alone reduces this source to add and remove detection, and its per-URL lastmod is the only thing that makes an EDIT to a page that already exists detectable at all. sitemapDated keeps every lastmod except those shared by three or more URLs at the same millisecond, which is the build stamp. The oscillating values all share one stamp; a real single-page edit does not. Activated 2026-08-31 after a double dry run in which the second consecutive run committed nothing.

The forecasting artifact. 13,410 bytes for the .md twin against 1,006,482 for the HTML page, which is why the .md URL is the archived one; minBytes is half the 13,410. contentType text because a markdown parse check is exactly as vacuous as a plain text one, so the canary carries the health check here. Non-numeric families exist (claude-fable-5, claude-mythos-preview), so no claude-(opus|sonnet|haiku)-N regex anywhere downstream. Eight or more further tables follow the master one.
63,970 bytes on 2026-08-26, so minBytes is half that. The llms-full.txt twin is excluded deliberately at 39,763,086 bytes per day.

66,545 bytes when spec section 4 was probed on 2026-08-26, so minBytes is half that; a second probe the same day read 69,285, so this file drifts and no size equality is asserted anywhere. The /docs/ path is load bearing and the two files were measured side by side on 2026-08-26: openrouter.ai/docs/llms.txt is 69,285 bytes, md5 32a32f3aa92fae497c7addebe303c6c7, opening '# OpenRouter | Documentation', while openrouter.ai/llms.txt is 72,739 bytes, md5 2a015c6c8ae672e20cac55541a96f38e, opening '# OpenRouter'. Different files, not a redirect.

Predicate is extracted over sitemapLoc, the loc set only. This sitemap is not static: cache-control is public, max-age=0, must-revalidate and cf-cache-status is DYNAMIC. It is rebuilt several times a day, rewriting about 100 lastmod values per rebuild independent of any content change, so a bytes predicate would commit 617 KB of build noise every run into a history that is never rewritten. This is the same treatment already given to platform.claude.com/sitemap.xml. Unlike anthropic-sitemap the loc set is the whole signal here, because the per-URL lastmod is rewritten wholesale rather than per edit, so there is no edit signal in it to preserve. retries 3 rather than the usual 2 because a curl (35) connection reset was observed against this host. Activated 2026-08-31 after a double dry run in which the second consecutive run committed nothing; the two probe bodies were in fact byte-identical, 4,973 locs each.

34,432 bytes on 2026-08-26, so minBytes is half that. This host is deliberate and unobvious: platform.openai.com/llms.txt 404s, and platform.openai.com/docs/llms.txt is a 301 to this URL whose own 81-byte body is the redirect text, which a collector that does not follow redirects would archive instead of the file. That 81-byte body is caught by minBytes and by the size band, never by parsing.

797,252 bytes on 2026-08-26, so minBytes is half that, and timeoutS 90 rather than 60 for the size. This is the full-text file rather than an index because Groq ships zero .md twins, so it is the only path to Groq content diffs. That also makes it the source the proportional hold rule exists for: one Groq docs-platform migration is a whole-file rewrite with nothing to threshold on.

Predicate is extracted over sorted table blocks. bytes is wrong here because the file's rows re-permute per request, so it would commit 1.46 MB of pure permutation daily forever, and mask cannot express it because a reordering is not a maskable substring. Sorting in the deriver cannot fix it either: the deriver only ever sees what was committed, and the commit decision is upstream of it, so the predicate itself has to express sort equality. The sorted md5 b92fafe614002915ea5a5b5e5be3060b reproduced across three independent captures hours apart while every raw md5 differed. Of the two conflicting measurements the narrower is adopted: 12 changed lines and 270 differing bytes across 6 runs, adjacent row swaps inside two pricing tables, which is what argues for sorting WITHIN table blocks rather than over the whole file. Sorting the whole file would make a legitimate section reorder invisible. Re-measured 2026-08-31: two fetches differed in exactly 6 lines, all of them row swaps inside three tables, and the xai projection was equal. Header and delimiter rows keep their positions, so a renamed column is still a change. Activated 2026-08-31 after a double dry run in which the second consecutive run committed nothing.

The repository is anomalyco/models.dev, not sst/models.dev. 20 entries, 20,239 bytes, no API rate limit, so minBytes is half the recorded size. The observed 20-entry window spanned 24m29s, so a daily poll loses commits and even a fast tier could; O3 resolves that with git fetch rather than a tier move, which is why this stays daily. freshness feed/7 rather than the incident feeds' 120 because this is an activity feed that cycles its whole window in under half an hour, so a week of silence means the feed or the repo is dead, not that the project is quiet. sizeBand widened to [0.4, 3.0] because a fixed count window of 20 commits sizes with how verbose the messages are, which is not a content integrity signal.

Predicate is mask, not bytes. 25 entries, all carrying published, newest 2026-08-24T20:26:21Z. Downstream must key on published and not updated: 16 of the 25 share a bulk backfill updated of 2026-08-14. The mask covers the feed-level updated element and nothing else. That line advances per cache generation while every entry stays byte-identical, and it has already produced seven commits whose entire content is one timestamp moving: commits 3a80c22 and 690dd60, 49 minutes apart, differ in that line alone across two 33,787-byte captures. The pattern is a negative lookbehind for an opening entry tag rather than an indentation match, so it selects the one updated element that precedes the first entry and can never reach an entry's own updated: measured on the archived body, 1 masked and all 25 entry updated elements left in place. freshness feed/120 because a provider with a genuinely good quarter publishes no incidents for 60+ days, and a daily failure mail for that is how alerting channels get muted; a stale feed is stale, not failed, and does not drive the exit code. minBytes is deliberately a stub catcher at 1,024 bytes, which an empty or error body cannot clear.

Predicate is extracted over atomStatus, not bytes. Measured 2026-08-26: six fetches gave two distinct md5s at an identical 92,282 bytes. Two things move per cache generation and neither is an incident. The feed-level updated re-stamps, and the affected-component list inside every entry is permuted, 493 differing runs across 15,600 bytes, while entry id order and set stay stable. atomStatus projects each entry's id, its updated, and its component list SORTED. Sorting kills the permutation while leaving a component APPEARING or VANISHING visible, which is the quiet withdrawal a status feed exists to leak; dropping the component list would be cheaper and would throw that away. The feed-level updated sits outside every entry and so is never read. This feed carries zero published elements, only updated, which is why freshness reads the entry-scoped date rather than the document-wide one. Activated 2026-08-31 after a double dry run in which the second consecutive run committed nothing.
